scope: Desktop Chrome History API control using plain HTML. No Pletina product code, physical Android input, installed PWA or operating-system Home/minimize action is tested.
setup: Open a real /outside document on an ephemeral loopback HTTP origin.
Open /control on that origin and click its real button to give the document a user activation.
Replace the current history state with {step:'boundary'} and push {step:'home'} at the same control URL.
Observe History API calls, Navigation API navigate events and popstate; do not intercept or change traversal behavior.
Wait 300 ms after issuing the calls, inspect the resulting document/state, and close the page.

cases.sequence: Install a once-only popstate listener that records call-2 and calls history.back(); then record call-1 and call history.back().

result: Both desktop programmatic sequences produced two accepted traversals and reached the preceding document. This control did not reproduce coalescence and cannot establish what happens to a very fast physical Xiaomi Back gesture.
